pr.title: Change a setting through project config set
pr.head: 3156d83178968a6cb56aece6a29266967bc59e03

summary: Projector reads its settings from .projector.toml files. It merges them from your home directory, ~/.projector.toml, down to the repository's own file, and the nearest file wins. project config could only read those settings, so changing one meant editing TOML by hand.

This pull request adds project config set <key> <value> and project config unset <key>. Both change one file: the repository's own .projector.toml by default, ~/.projector.toml with --user, or any file with --file. The editor works on lines, so it keeps your comments and layout, and it checks its own result before and after it writes.

A new schema, SETTINGS, lists every key Projector reads and its type. set accepts only those keys. unset also removes a key outside the schema when the file sets it, so you can clean up a setting Projector no longer reads. The existing readers that check a value's type now go through the same schema.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Layer: one .projector.toml file in the merge. The user layer is ~/.projector.toml; the repository's file is the nearest layer.
  • SETTINGS: the map from each key Projector reads to its type, bool or str.
  • Change: what one write did, with an action of set, unset, or unchanged.
  • Override note: the stderr line that names a nearer file whose value wins over the one just written.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first Projector review, of e305e65, found that set skipped the override note when the value was already in the file. 55104e5 fixed it, and the thread is resolved.
  • Later commits let unset remove a key outside the schema, refuse a --file in a missing directory, and drop integer handling from the schema.
  • The full review of 84a9073 is clean. Its one suggestion was that unset on a whole table blamed an inline table. 3156d83 refuses a table key with its own message, and an incremental review of that head is clean.

groups.title: A settings schema and a line editor
groups.kicker: SETTINGS names each key and its type; write_value changes one key's line
intro: Before this change, each reader of a typed setting checked the type itself, with its own copy of the error message. SETTINGS in src/projector/config.py now holds every key Projector reads, the ones skills read with project config get included.

Config.setting(key) returns the merged value, or None when no layer sets it, and raises ConfigError, exit code 78, when a file holds a value of another type. parse_value turns command-line text into the key's type for set.
Python's standard library reads TOML with tomllib but cannot write it, and rewriting the whole file would lose a person's comments. So write_value edits the text:

1. Scan. _scan walks the lines and records each table header and each key = value statement, with the table it belongs to. A statement that spans lines, such as a multi-line string, ends at the first run of lines that parses on its own.
  2. Edit. A key that is set gets its new value on the same line, and any comment after the value stays. A missing key goes after the last statement of its table, or beside the dotted keys that define the table. A missing table goes at the end of the file. unset deletes the key's lines. unset_value refuses a key outside the schema that the file does not set, so a misspelled key gets the list of keys. Both commands refuse a key that names a table, such as review, because they change one setting.
  3. Check before writing. The new text must parse, give the key its new value, and leave every other value unchanged. Otherwise the command refuses with exit code 65 and the file untouched, as for a key inside an inline table.
  4. Write and read back. write_through replaces the file's content and keeps a symlink a link. The editor then reads the file back and restores the original when the check fails.

checks.text: Every key that src/ reads and every key a skill reads with project config get is in SETTINGS, with the type its readers expect. Checked by searching src/, skills/, and docs/ for reads.

Edits of 18 hand-written files changed only the key's line or refused with the file untouched. The cases included a header with a trailing comment, quoted and dotted keys, a subtable with no parent header, CRLF line endings, a missing final newline, a multi-line array with an inner comment, an array of tables, and control characters in a value. Run against e305e65 in a scratch directory. The editor has not changed since that head.

files.note: The schema, the typed reader, and the line editor that set and unset use. The editor is the second group.

groups.title: The set and unset commands
groups.kicker: Which file the commands change, what they print, and the override note
intro: change_config in src/projector/cli.py picks the file, calls write_value for set or unset_value for unset, and prints the result as a line or, with --json, as an object with action, key, old, new, and file.

config_file chooses the file. --file wins, then --user, then the repository root from --root or Git. A --file in a directory that does not exist exits 2, so a mistyped path creates nothing. Outside a repository with neither option, the command exits 69. After the write, report_override loads the merged configuration and prints the override note when the effective value differs from the one written, or says the file is not read here. It runs after every action, unchanged included.
The same file also moves six readers, such as site_enabled and configured_prepare, onto Config.setting.

checks.text: With HOME and the working directory in scratch directories, the command wrote the right file from a repository subdirectory, with --user, and with a relative --file. It exited 2 for a --file in a missing directory, exited 69 outside a repository, and refused --user with --file.

files.note: Adds the set and unset parsers, the file choice, the override note, and moves the typed readers onto Config.setting.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: ConfigSetTests drives the commands through main in a temporary repository
intro: ConfigSetTests creates a Git repository under a temporary home directory and patches HOME, so no test touches your own configuration. A final test checks that the key table in docs/cli.md matches SETTINGS.

checks.text: The 48 config tests pass at this head on Python 3.12. The full suite, 946 tests, passed at 84a9073, and only config.py, its tests, and docs/cli.md changed after that.

groups.title: Documentation and skills
groups.kicker: The docs show the command where they told you to edit a file
intro: docs/cli.md gains a "Change configuration" section and says that only the keys in its table can be set. The other documents, and the two review skills, now show project config set where they told you to write a key by hand. The skills still say that the user decides to turn summaries off.

checks.text: project config set with no option changes the repository's .projector.toml, which is usually a tracked file. docs/plugins.md suggests --user for watch.auto_start for that reason.
